sources.title: Aprea Therapeutics Form 10-Q for the quarter ended 30 September 2026
sources.access_scope: Full company-hosted HTML text retrieved; review focused on reporting period, signatures, APR-246 status, and research-and-development expense disclosure.
observations: The report covers the quarter ended 30 September 2026 and is signed 4 November 2026.
The company reports no ongoing clinical trials involving APR-246.
Its nine-month expense comparison reports an increase of approximately US$0.1 million in APR-246 costs related to patent maintenance, regulatory and program closeout activities.
sources.inference: Company clinical inactivity does not establish abandoned intellectual property or an available license. The source supplies no ddiscov transaction price or available economic interest.
limitations: Company-reported statements, not an independent patent-title or freedom-to-operate audit.
Does not establish absence of all investigator-initiated activity globally.
The expense increase is not the total program cost or a licensing quote.

sources.title: Salois et al., A Novel Model System to Identify Cellular and Molecular Defects Underlying Rare Genetic Disorders
sources.access_scope: Full HTML main text and figure legends; parent review focused on expression controls, disease phenotype, treatment scope and data availability. Linked supplement separately recovered by advancement agent.
observations: The engineered AEC model includes an ectopic wild-type TP63 control at similar total-expression levels. Authors report no observed differences between this control and untransduced cells in the examined adhesion, migration and tissue-architecture comparisons.
Total TP63 remains approximately twice the untransduced-cell level. A matched control addresses one concern but does not prove native physiology or exclude all artifacts.
The paper establishes disease-relevant cellular and tissue phenotypes, not APR-246 rescue of an established barrier defect.
The data-availability statement offers supporting data on reasonable request; no access or transfer was obtained.
sources.inference: Full-text recovery improves the documentary basis for considering an existing model while leaving treatment response, clinical product fit and executable access unresolved.
limitations: No treatment efficacy or model-transfer validation was generated.
No observed difference is not formal equivalence.
Cell-matrix adhesion and tissue architecture are not complete mature-barrier function.

sources.title: US12521392B2 official patent-publication record
sources.access_scope: Returned official-publication bibliographic record and all eight claims. No current assignment-chain or legal-status audit, and no facsimile inspection.
observations: The record identifies US12521392B2, application 17/258894, eight claims, and publication on 13 January 2026.
Claim 1 combines AEC, PRIMA-1MET and an ectodermal-dysplasia condition affecting at least one cornea.
Dependent cream and skin-erosion claims refer to claim 1 and retain its limitations.
The publication lists INSERM, Universite de Paris and AP-HP as assignees. These bibliographic names are not a current-title opinion.
sources.inference: Official-source recovery strengthens provenance for the existing claim-scope caution. Topical skin administration alone does not resolve the patient-predicate question or establish commercial clearance.
limitations: No freedom-to-operate, infringement, enforceability or licensing conclusion.
No ownership chain or current European status established.
Patent examples do not add independent treated people to the underlying clinical evidence.

sources.title: Dai et al., Chemogenetic Neuromodulation for Refractory Epilepsy
sources.access_scope: Direct publisher abstract, publication history, author affiliations and supplementary-material names. Subscriber gateway excludes the clinical letter body; no full-text audit is claimed.
observations: The publisher abstract describes three patients and a mean seizure-frequency reduction of 92.6% during treatment with hippocampal chemogenetic therapy and clozapine.
Abstract adverse events are described as grade 1 or 2.
The page identifies a protocol and supplementary appendix but this read does not recover their bodies.
sources.inference: The clinical signal remains a consequential information priority. This abstract does not provide a controlled effect, uncommon-safety estimate, expanded cohort or investable economic interest.
sources.access_change: Direct abstract retrieved rather than relying only on search-indexed text; clinical full-text limitation remains.
limitations: No expanded patient count inferred from institutional program totals.
No detailed adverse-event table, protocol or supplementary outcome analysis read in this parent check.
No login, subscription, purchase or access-control circumvention occurred.

sources.title: A small-molecule stabilizer of the calpastatin–calpain-2 complex restores mitochondrial function and mitigates neurodegeneration
sources.access_scope: Full primary main text, figure legends, discussion, conflict disclosure and data/material availability; linked supporting files not independently audited by root.
observations: A36 is a CHIR99021-derived CAST–calpain-2 interaction stabilizer; the paper reports rescue in HD patient-derived neurons and motor/striatal outcomes in R6/2 mice.
PS19 tauopathy results are a separate model context, not an HD replication or treated-human cohort.
The paper identifies remaining pharmacokinetic optimization and chronic safety questions, and discloses a CWRU provisional filing, US63/662,559, with PCT pending.
sources.inference: The combination of functional animal evidence and patient-derived neuronal evidence supports bounded information priority within this new screen; it does not establish a clinically ready or obtainable asset.
limitations: No human therapeutic efficacy or all-in development quote.
Patent disclosure is not verification of current title, claim status, freedom to operate or license availability.
Root repeat inspection is the same evidence family as the screening agent's primary paper.
sources.retrieval_method: Firecrawl scrape; independent root source check

sources.title: Repurposing the HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor atorvastatin for SRD5A3-congenital disorder of glycosylation
sources.access_scope: Full primary main text, figure legends and discussion; parent review focused on functional versus biochemical endpoints and inference limits.
observations: The study reports improved disease-related worm phenotypes and analyzes fibroblasts from four affected individuals.
The patient-fibroblast polyprenol/dolichol ratio moved toward rescue in three of four lines, with a nonsignificant group comparison, p=0.08.
Worm functional changes did not establish normalization of the measured polyprenol/dolichol metabolites; biochemical, glycosylation and clinical benefit claims must remain distinct.
sources.inference: A narrower evidence claim is warranted than the abstract's broad rescue language. The exact SRD5A3 use can be screened while the molecule remains previously encountered.
limitations: Four patient-derived cell lines are not four treated patients.
No established correction of glycosylation or human disease benefit.
Final paper and earlier preprint belong to one study lineage; duplicate retrieval is not replication.
sources.retrieval_method: Firecrawl scrape; independent root source check

sources.title: Pharmacological rescue of mitochondrial dysfunction, neurite degeneration, and premature death of ALS and AD iPSC-derived neurons
sources.access_scope: Full preprint main text and figure legends, discussion and disclosures. Supplementary evidence described in main text is distinguished from direct supplementary-file inspection.
observations: The principal C9/ISO iPSC pair supports several neuronal endpoints; the main text also reports mitochondrial and neurite parameter findings in three additional C9 lines from different ALS patients, citing figure S6.
The study includes an engineered TARDBP M337V context. Additional cell contexts do not establish that every endpoint replicated across all backgrounds.
The authors describe conflicting CNS-penetration evidence and ongoing in-vivo ALS work; they disclose related US17/756,842 and PCT/US26/15790 applications and a Mitochondrial Medicines interest.
sources.inference: The screen should not describe the entire paper as confined to one patient lineage, but it must keep endpoint-specific replication and the preprint/in-vitro boundary explicit.
limitations: No treated-human ALS benefit or completed in-vivo ALS efficacy established by this paper.
A known approved drug does not establish sufficient exposure for this intended CNS use.
Disclosed patent applications are not available licenses or current legal opinions.
sources.retrieval_method: Firecrawl scrape; independent root source check

sources.title: ChiCTR2500111157: chemogenetic therapy for temporal-lobe epilepsy with unilateral hippocampal sclerosis
sources.access_scope: Full bilingual primary registry record, independently read for planned enrollment, dates, design and blinding. This is a design record, not trial results.
observations: The record was registered and last refreshed on 27 October 2025 and labels its registration retrospective.
It describes a single arm, a planned sample size of six, no randomization and a blinding field of None.
The recorded execution period is 8 January 2025 to 7 January 2030 and recruitment period 9 January to 31 December 2025; these planned dates do not establish actual completion or current status.
sources.inference: The registry supports a planned-six interpretation, not six verified treated participants or a nine-person pooled cohort. Blinded-assessor institutional wording requires protocol-level clarification and is not necessarily inconsistent with an open-label intervention.
limitations: No verified all-treated safety denominator.
No current recruitment or completion claim from stale fields.
Same record independently read by reassessment agent; not independent clinical evidence.

sources.title: Encapsulation of AAVs into Protein Vault Nanoparticles as a Novel Solution to Gene Therapy's Neutralizing Antibody Problem
sources.access_scope: Full main text and figure legends; independent root check of serum origin, cultured-cell setting and comparator interpretation.
observations: Neutralizing serum came from immunized mice and the principal transduction comparison used cultured CHO-Lec2 cells.
Vault-packaged AAV retained transduction in the neutralizing-serum comparison, whereas the unpackaged mixture showed low transduction.
Without neutralizing serum, both packaged and unpackaged mixtures enhanced transduction; baseline uptake therefore does not uniquely establish packaging-mediated shielding.
sources.inference: The known paper supports a platform reserve while leaving human immune escape, clinical benefit and in-vivo repeat dosing unestablished.
limitations: No new efficacy study or clinical result added by this repeated read.
Universal immune invisibility is not established.
Current ownership and attainable rights were not verified in this source check.
